Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - DetectArchiverTestCase.testCOMPRESS335 simply tries to obtain an ArchiveInputStream for the file “COMPRESS-335.tar”.
  - This triggers TAR header parsing and checksum verification as part of TAR detection.

- Parsing flow:
  - TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry reads a 512-byte header block and constructs a TarArchiveEntry from it.
  - TarArchiveEntry.parseTarHeader delegates checksum verification to TarUtils.verifyCheckSum(header) and records the result in checkSumOK.

- The checksum verification logic (TarUtils.verifyCheckSum):
  - It walks through the header and, for the checksum field (CHKSUM_OFFSET..CHKSUM_OFFSET+CHKSUMLEN), it:
    - Accumulates a storedSum from octal digits it encounters.
    - Critically, it only accumulates the first six octal digits due to the condition digits++ < 6.
    - After processing each byte in the checksum field, it substitutes the byte with a space when summing the header for unsignedSum/signedSum, which is standard practice.
  - Finally it returns whether storedSum equals the computed unsignedSum or signedSum.

- Why this fails for COMPRESS-335:
  - The provided archive has a right-aligned checksum: the 8-byte checksum field is filled entirely with octal digits (leading zeros on the left), with no trailing NUL-space terminator.
  - TarUtils.verifyCheckSum assumes there are at most six meaningful octal digits and ignores any additional digits by truncating the parsed checksum to the first six digits found.
  - In a right-aligned, fully digit-filled field, the true checksum uses all 8 octal digits. By parsing only the first six, the method drops the last two digits (“the last two digits of the stored checksum are lost”), yielding a smaller storedSum.
  - The computed header sums (unsignedSum/signedSum) represent the actual checksum; since storedSum is truncated, neither comparison matches and verifyCheckSum returns false.

- Consequences and link to the test failure:
  - parseTarHeader sets checkSumOK to false.
  - The TAR detector relies on a valid header checksum; with an invalid checksum, the format detection fails or the header is rejected, causing the test’s attempt to obtain a TAR stream for “COMPRESS-335.tar” to fail.

- Root cause:
  - TarUtils.verifyCheckSum incorrectly limits parsing of the checksum field to the first six octal digits, an assumption that breaks for valid TARs that use all 8 digits with right alignment and no trailing NUL/space terminator.
  - Since the method already validates each byte as an octal digit before accumulating it, restricting to six digits is unnecessary and causes truncation. The method should parse all consecutive octal digits present within the checksum field (up to the field length), not just the first six.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
